tasks.spec:
You are an implementation worker. Write exactly ONE Python file in your current working directory: ./outro_match_master.py. READ access to /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast; never write to it. No git, no MCP, no network. Pure stdlib + numpy + ffmpeg/ffprobe subprocess.

GOAL. A podcast owner wants spoken audio FULLY mastered to match the sonic character of a reference music outro he loves: spectral shape, harmonic richness, dynamics feel, and stereo/spatial character. A damage-removal chain already exists and is the fallback; this tool is the full-transfer version. It must be deterministic, measured, and self-verifying -- a receipt, not vibes.

FILE CONTRACT: ./outro_match_master.py with argparse CLI:
  outro_match_master.py profile --reference PATH --out-profile PROFILE.json
  outro_match_master.py master --input PATH --profile PROFILE.json --out PATH [--max-band-db 8] [--json REPORT.json]

PROFILE mode analyzes the reference once and writes a JSON profile containing:
  (a) SPECTRAL: mean power in 24 log-spaced bands from 50Hz to 16kHz (Welch PSD, 4096-point Hann, 50% overlap, mono-summed), stored as dB per band plus the band edges;
  (b) DYNAMICS: short-term loudness variance -- compute RMS in 400ms hops, store the standard deviation in dB (the 'movement' of the reference) and the crest factor (peak-to-RMS dB);
  (c) SPATIAL: stereo width = side-channel energy over mid-channel energy in dB (mid=(L+R)/2, side=(L-R)/2); mono references store -inf/None;
  (d) LOUDNESS: integrated LUFS via ffmpeg loudnorm print_format=json.

MASTER mode applies, in THIS order (each stage a named function, chain built as one ffmpeg filtergraph where possible, two ffmpeg passes allowed):
  1. MATCH-EQ: measure the input's 24-band spectrum the same way; per-band gain = reference_band_db - input_band_db, normalized so the mean gain across bands is 0 (loudness is handled separately, only SHAPE transfers), each band CLAMPED to +/-max-band-db (default 8). Emit an ffmpeg firequalizer gain_entry curve from the band centers/gains (interpolated). This is the true spectral transfer.
  2. HARMONIC: aexciter, with amount scaled by the REMAINING high-band deficit after EQ (bands above 6kHz): deficit 0dB -> amount 0 (skip stage), deficit >=6dB -> amount 3, linear in between. Never apply blindly.
  3. DYNAMICS MATCH: if the input's short-term RMS std-dev exceeds the reference's by more than 1.5dB, apply acompressor (attack 8ms, release 180ms, knee 3dB) with ratio chosen from the excess (excess 1.5-3dB -> ratio 2:1, >3dB -> 3:1, capped at 3:1); if the input is ALREADY less dynamic than the reference, skip compression (never expand).
  4. DE-ESS: a -3dB bell at 6.8kHz Q~3 AFTER the brightening stages.
  5. SPATIAL: if the reference has stereo width and the input is effectively mono/narrow, apply stereotools with a bounded side-level lift toward the reference width, capped at +6dB side gain, mono-compatibility preserved (never invert phase, never delay one channel -- no Haas tricks, they break mono downmix).
  6. FINISH: alimiter=0.95, then two-pass LINEAR loudnorm to I=-16:TP=-1.5 (measure pass then apply pass with measured_* values; if ffmpeg reports normalization_type dynamic, raise -- do not ship a squashed result).

SELF-VERIFICATION (mandatory, in master mode): re-measure the OUTPUT's 24 bands and report per-band residual vs the reference profile; report the mean absolute residual BEFORE (input vs ref) and AFTER (output vs ref); if AFTER mean-abs-residual is not at least 30% smaller than BEFORE, exit 1 with a clear message (the transfer failed to converge); print a compact table: band_hz, ref_db, in_db, out_db, residual. Also report output LUFS, short-term std-dev vs ref, and width vs ref. Write everything to --json when given. Exit 2 on unusable inputs.

No hard-coded episode paths or names; everything from CLI. Fail loudly. Keep every threshold a named constant with a one-line rationale.
